title: RAG4GFM: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Graph Foundation Models through Graph

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (9) and the surrounding text describing graph-level fusion in Section 3.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (9) defines β_v^i = SOFTMAX( h_v · (h_g^q + h_g^i) ), where h_v is a node feature vector (dimension d) and h_g^q, h_g^i are graph-level embeddings formed by concatenating node, edge, and statistical features (dimension d + d_e + 3). The dot product between vectors of different dimensionalities is undefined, making the equation invalid.

Table 1 lists the datasets for node classification/link prediction as Books-Children, Books-History, Ele-Computers, Ele-Photo. However, Table 2 and the accompanying text in Section 4.2 refer to results on 'Fitness' (e.g., 'Fitness Acc', 'Fitness ROC-AUC', 'Fitness Recall'). No 'Fitness' dataset is described in the paper, creating a direct contradiction between the documented datasets and the reported results.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract vs. Section 3.1 and Appendix A.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states that RAG4GFM 'achiev[es] efficient constant-time retrieval and fusion for all graph sizes'. Section 3.1 states that the index guarantees O(log₂ N) retrieval and fusion, and Appendix A.1 derives an overall per-query time of O(log N + k|V|²) (dense) or O(log N + k|E|) (sparse). Constant-time performance is impossible with O(log N) retrieval and graph-size-dependent fusion, so the abstract claim directly conflicts with the method's own analysis.

The abstract asserts that RAG4GFM 'achiev[es] near-perfect accuracy in all tested scenarios'. The highest accuracy reported in the paper is 87.34% (GLEM+RAG4GFM on Computers, Table 2), and other tasks are substantially lower (e.g., 65.51% graph classification). 'Near-perfect' implies accuracy close to 100%, which is grossly misaligned with the actual experimental results.

The text states: 'For instance, GLEM+RAG4GFM achieves 83.12% accuracy on node classification in the Computers dataset'. However, Table 2 reports GLEM+RAG4GFM node classification accuracy on Computers as 87.34%. This is a direct numerical contradiction between the textual claim and the presented results table.

Section 3.1 claims that the hierarchical indexing 'guarantees efficient O(log₂ N) end-to-end retrieval and fusion time for all graph sizes and densities'. However, Appendix A.1 shows that the graph fusion enhancement module alone costs O(k|V|²) or O(k|E|) time, making the overall end-to-end per-query time O(log N + k|V|²) or O(log N + k|E|). The claim that the entire pipeline (including fusion) is O(log N) independent of graph size is factually incorrect according to the paper's own complexity analysis.
